newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro says equity issue a last resort.
newsitem.headline: Vitro says equity issue a last resort.

text.p: Mexican glassmaker Vitro is considering a $100-150 million equity issue or convertible bond placement as a last resort to pay down debt, Finance Director Hugo Jaime Garcia said on Monday.

"Let's say this alternative is being looked at as the final option," he said, referring to the company's plans to pay down $300 million in debt this year, lowering it to $1.5 billion from $1.8 billion.

On Monday, Libbey Inc said it agreed in principal to pay $100 million in cash to Vitro to become a 49 percent equity holder in its glass tableware division, Vitrocrisa, and to purchase flatware supplier WorldCrisa.
That money would go toward paying down debt.
Garcia said lowering the debt by $300 million would shave some $45 million a year off interest payments.
He also said the firm planned to change its mix of debt to 55 percent in dollars and 45 percent in pesos.
